title: Taking From Either End of a Row

concept.title: Score the position as "my total minus the opponent's total"
body: A row of numbers lies on the table. The players take turns; in a turn you remove the number at the **left end** or at the **right end** and add it to your score. Both want the largest possible difference between their own score and the opponent's. Instead of tracking two scores, define `best(i, j)` as the **best difference** (current player minus the other) the player to move can achieve on the part `a[i..j]`.

If you take `a[i]`, the opponent faces `a[i+1..j]` and gets `best(i + 1, j)` more than you from there, so your difference is `a[i] - best(i + 1, j)`. Taking `a[j]` gives `a[j] - best(i, j - 1)`. You choose the larger:

The "minus" is the trick: the same function describes the opponent, whose gain is your loss. There are only `n * n` different parts `a[i..j]`, so with a memo the search is quick even for 40 numbers, where trying all `2^40` games would be impossible.

statement: A row has `n` non-negative integers. Two players take turns; in each turn the player removes the number at the left end or at the right end of the row and adds it to their own score. The first player starts. Both play to maximise (their own score minus the other score). Print the largest difference the first player can guarantee (it can be negative).
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` integers.

examples.note: The first player takes 1. Whatever the second player takes (5 or 7), the first player then takes 233: 1 + 233 against 5 + 7 is a difference of 222.

hints: Define best(i, j) as the best difference (mover minus the other) on the part a[i..j].
Taking the left end gives a[i] minus best(i + 1, j); taking the right end gives a[j] minus best(i, j - 1).
Store the values in a table: there are only n * n different parts.

explanation: `best(i, j)` is the larger of `a[i] - best(i + 1, j)` and `a[j] - best(i, j - 1)`: the mover takes an end and then plays the opponent role on the rest. The empty part is worth 0, and each of the `n * n` parts is computed once.
